summary: NO SOURCE FOR THIS ROADMAP EXISTS IN THE SUPPLIED LIBRARY. This job therefore downloaded four papers from arXiv on 2026-09-16, using the URLs printed in the roadmap's own source-label dictionary (content/campaign/NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa/README.md lines 129-134), recorded their sha256 hashes, and kept them in a scratch directory outside the repository: CFKSV arXiv:math/0404297, Kakde arXiv:1008.0142v3, Ritter-Weiss arXiv:1004.2578 (downloaded, NOT read) and Burns-Venjakob arXiv:math/0511672. CFKSV Sec. 2 was read IN FULL WITH ALL PROOFS, which is why NE.1 is the only stage marked source_decomposed: the canonical Ore set S, the four equivalent characterizations at a pro-p level, the two-sided Ore property, the non-zero-divisor property, and Schneider's characterization of S as the elements regular modulo the preimage of the prime radical. The central Z_p subgroup Pi of G/J and the finite-dimensional algebra V(G/J) over the commutative field R(Pi) are the machinery that makes all four characterizations equivalent, and they are recorded rather than packaged. Three findings. (1) CFKSV's whole framework rests on TWO standing hypotheses - G has a closed normal H with G/H isomorphic to Z_p, and (for the K-theory) G has no element of order p - and the paper says explicitly that the forthcoming Fukaya-Kato work removes both. (2) Kakde's uniqueness holds in K_1', NOT in K_1, and he warns that in CFKSV, Fukaya-Kato, Burns-Flach, Huber-Kings and Ritter-Weiss the zeta function is conjectured in K_1 'and hence uniqueness may not hold'; the bridge is Burns's computation SK_1(Lambda(G)_S) = Ker(partial) intersect the intersection of the kernels of all Artin evaluations, which is exactly the SK_1 ambiguity the NE.3 stage asks to exhibit. (3) The boundary-map signs look different: CFKSV write partial_G(xi_M) = +[M] for a module, and Kakde writes partial(zeta) = -[C] for a complex. [Corrected in review REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16: this is NOT a conflict of boundary-map conventions. Both sources' boundary maps send a denominator element to the class of the cokernel of multiplication by it (CFKSV proof of Lemma 4.6, printed p. 24; Kakde Sec. 2.2, printed p. 7). Kakde's minus sign belongs to the complex C(F_infinity/F), which has X in degree -1 and Z_p in degree 0. His abelian Theorem 16 (printed pp. 15-16) derives partial(zeta) = -[C] from Wiles's theorem, where it reads [X] - [Z_p]. The degree convention in Kakde's identification of the relative K_0 with complexes is not written out on p. 7, so the dictionary still has to be stated.] Fukaya-Kato's original formulation, Burns's SK_1 paper, and the 2025/2026 Ritter-Weiss and abelian sources could not be obtained. NE.4 is not_read; every other stage is partial except NE.1. [Review REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16: all four arXiv PDFs were re-fetched and their SHA-256 hashes match. Further corrections: the CFKSV page locators for Sec. 2, Theorem 2.4, Proposition 3.4, Theorem 4.4 and Sec. 5 were one page early. The claim that surjectivity of the boundary map REQUIRES G to have no element of order p is contradicted by Kakde Lemma 5 (printed p. 8), which proves surjectivity onto the relative K_0 without that hypothesis. Conjecture 5.7 is stated by CFKSV only after assuming analytic continuation of L(E,rho,s) and Deligne's period conjecture (103), with the R-truncated L-function and Deligne's epsilon-factor normalizations. For G = Z_p the set S is NOT all nonzero elements: p is not in S, and S^* is the set of nonzero elements. The link from SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 was removed as unverified.]

nodes.title: Lambda(G) and Omega(G) as inverse limits, and the two standing hypotheses on G
nodes.statement: For G a compact p-adic Lie group set Lambda(G) = inverse limit over open normal subgroups U of Z_p[G/U] and Omega(G) = inverse limit over U of F_p[G/U]. Both are left and right Noetherian. If Lambda(G) has no zero divisors (for example if G is pro-p with no element of order p) one writes Q(G) for the skew field of fractions. THE WHOLE CFKSV FRAMEWORK ASSUMES a closed normal subgroup H of G with Gamma = G/H isomorphic to Z_p. For an open subgroup H' of H, Lambda(H) is FREE of rank [H : H'] over Lambda(H') on either side, so finite generation over Lambda(H) and over Lambda(H') are equivalent. For J an open normal (in G) pro-p subgroup of H, Lambda(J) is a LOCAL ring whose maximal ideal is the kernel of the augmentation Lambda(J) -> F_p, so Nakayama's lemma is available.
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group; Lambda(G) and Omega(G) are Noetherian on both sides (CFKSV state this as well known and do not prove it)
The absence of zero divisors is asserted only under a hypothesis such as 'G pro-p with no element of order p'; it is NOT a consequence of compactness

The existence of H with G/H isomorphic to Z_p is a STANDING HYPOTHESIS (2) of the paper, not a derived fact. CFKSV note that the forthcoming Fukaya-Kato work removes both this and the no-p-torsion hypothesis
Freeness of Lambda(H) over Lambda(H') needs H' OPEN in H

CFKSV assert locality of Lambda(J), with maximal ideal the kernel of Lambda(J) -> F_p, for J PRO-p. The converse (that the ring need not be local for a general open J) is an authored remark, not a source statement.
Given a pro-p open J one can always find J' open in J and NORMAL IN G, because the set of G-conjugates of J is finite
proofSteps: Define the two inverse limits and record the Noetherian property.
Record the freeness of Lambda(H) over Lambda(H') for H' open in H and the resulting equivalence of finite-generation conditions.
Record that for J pro-p, Lambda(J) is local with maximal ideal ker(Lambda(J) -> F_p), which is the form in which Nakayama is applied throughout Sec. 2.
Record the normalization trick producing a G-normal pro-p open subgroup of H.
acceptance: Recover O[[T]] for G = Z_p and identify the topological generator with 1+T
Compute Lambda(G/J) and Omega(G/J) for a concrete nonabelian finite quotient
Check that absence of p-torsion, torsion-freeness and pro-p are three different conditions: exhibit a group with p-torsion where the skew-field-of-fractions statement fails

nodes.title: The canonical set S and the four equivalent descriptions at a pro-p level
nodes.statement: Define S to be the set of f in Lambda(G) such that Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)f is a FINITELY GENERATED Lambda(H)-module. Let J be any pro-p open subgroup of H normal in G, with phi_J : Lambda(G) -> Lambda(G/J) and psi_J : Lambda(G) -> Omega(G/J) the natural surjections. Then S equals each of: (i) the f with Lambda(G/J)/Lambda(G/J)phi_J(f) finitely generated over Z_p; (ii) the f with Omega(G/J)/Omega(G/J)psi_J(f) finite; (iii) the f with right multiplication by psi_J(f) on Omega(G/J) injective; and, by the right-handed Lemma 2.2, the corresponding four conditions for right modules, in particular (iv) the f with LEFT multiplication by psi_J(f) on Omega(G/J) injective. Moreover a finitely generated Lambda(G)-module (left or right) is finitely generated over Lambda(H) IF AND ONLY IF it is S-torsion.
hypotheses: J must be PRO-p, OPEN in H and NORMAL in G

The equivalence (ii) <=> (iii) uses the existence of a subgroup Pi of G/J isomorphic to Z_p and CENTRAL in G/J, obtained by writing G/J as a semidirect product of the finite H/J with a lift of Gamma and taking an open subgroup of that lift acting trivially by conjugation

It uses that Omega(Pi) is isomorphic to F_p[[T]], so its quotient field R(Pi) is COMMUTATIVE and lies in the centre of the finite-dimensional algebra V(G/J) = R(Pi) tensor_{Omega(Pi)} Omega(G/J); linear algebra over a commutative field then converts injectivity into surjectivity
It also uses that Omega(G/J) has no finite Omega(G/J)-submodule
The left/right symmetry of Lemma 2.2 follows because multiplication in V(G/J) is R(Pi)-linear and V(G/J) is finite dimensional over R(Pi), so a one-sided inverse is two-sided
proofSteps: Replace H by J in the definition of S, using the freeness of Lambda(H) over Lambda(J).
For f in Lambda(G) and M = Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)f, compute M_J = Lambda(G/J)/Lambda(G/J)phi_J(f) and M/m_J M = Omega(G/J)/Omega(G/J)psi_J(f); Nakayama gives (i) and (ii).
Construct the central Pi and the algebra V(G/J); use that Omega(Pi) is a DVR with residue field F_p, so a finitely generated Omega(Pi)-module is torsion iff finite, to get (iii).
Lemma 2.2(iv): S consists of the f for which alpha_J(f) has a left inverse in V(G/J); by R(Pi)-linearity and finite dimensionality, z alpha_J(f) = 1 iff alpha_J(f) z = 1.

Proposition 2.3: if M is S-torsion pick generators x_i and f_i in S with f_i x_i = 0, giving a surjection from a finite sum of Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)f_i onto M, each of which is finitely generated over Lambda(H); conversely a finitely generated Lambda(H)-module is S-torsion.
acceptance: Check the cyclic quotient example G = Gamma = Z_p (so H = 1). Here S is the set of f in Z_p[[T]] NOT divisible by p (mu(f) = 0): for such f, Lambda/(f) is finitely generated over Z_p by Weierstrass preparation, while Lambda/(p) = F_p[[T]] is not. In particular p is not in S, as CFKSV note on printed p. 7, and S^* = union of p^n S is the set of all nonzero elements. [Corrected in review: the item previously asked to verify that S itself is the set of nonzero elements, which is false; the Weierstrass computation is the reviewer's.]

Exhibit a nonzero element outside S^* when H is nontrivial. For example, take G = H x Gamma = Z_p^2 and h a topological generator of H. Then Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)(h - 1) = Lambda(Gamma) is not finitely generated over Lambda(H), and neither is any quotient by p^n(h - 1). CFKSV printed p. 22 identify S in this case as the complement of the prime ideal (p, U). [Reworded in review: S already omits p when H = 1, so the meaningful test concerns S^*.]

nodes.title: S is a two-sided Ore set of non-zero divisors, equal to the elements regular modulo a canonical nilpotent-defined ideal
nodes.statement: The set S is multiplicatively closed and is a LEFT AND RIGHT Ore set in Lambda(G), and its elements are NON-ZERO DIVISORS in Lambda(G). Moreover, setting N to be the preimage in Lambda(G) of the prime radical N(Omega(G/J)) for any pro-p open G-normal J in H (independent of the choice by Lemma 2.5), S is exactly the set of elements of Lambda(G) that are REGULAR MODULO N. Since p is not in S, one also forms S^* = union over n >= 0 of p^n S, again a two-sided Ore set of non-zero divisors, with Lambda(G)_{S^*} = Lambda(G)_S[1/p]. M_H(G) denotes the category of finitely generated S^*-torsion Lambda(G)-modules; M is S^*-torsion iff M/M(p) is finitely generated over Lambda(H).
hypotheses: Multiplicative closure uses the exact sequence 0 -> Lambda(G)s_2/Lambda(G)s_1 s_2 -> Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)s_1 s_2 -> Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)s_2 -> 0 and finite generation of the two outer terms over Lambda(H)
The Ore condition itself follows from Proposition 2.3 applied to Lambda(G)/Lambda(G)f and Lambda(G)/f Lambda(G)

The non-zero-divisor property is proved at each finite level: it suffices that phi_J(f) is not a zero divisor in Lambda(G/J), which follows because its image in W(G/J) = Q(Pi) tensor_{Lambda(Pi)} Lambda(G/J) has a two-sided inverse

Lemma 2.5 (due to P. Schneider) needs that Delta = J'/J is a FINITE NORMAL p-SUBGROUP of G/J, and the argument that Delta acts trivially on any simple V(G/J)-module because E^Delta is nonzero (p-group acting on a characteristic-p vector space) and is a submodule
p is CENTRAL in Lambda(G), which is what makes S^* an Ore set
proofSteps: Multiplicative closure from the displayed exact sequence.
Ore condition from Proposition 2.3: for f in S and x in Lambda(G) there are s, s' in S with sx in Lambda(G)f and xs' in f Lambda(G).
Non-zero divisors: pass to Lambda(G/J), form W(G/J), and use Lemma 2.1(i) with Lemma 2.2(ii) to invert the image of phi_J(f) on both sides.

Lemma 2.5: the kernel of Omega(G/J) -> Omega(G/J') is generated as a left ideal by the delta - 1 for delta in Delta; reduce to showing this lies in the prime radical, i.e. that Delta acts trivially on every simple V(G/J)-module, which holds because E^Delta is a nonzero submodule.

Proposition 2.6: f is regular mod N iff psi_J(f) becomes a unit in V(G/J)/N(V(G/J)); units modulo nilpotent ideals are units; combine with Lemma 2.1(iii) and the left-multiplication criterion. CFKSV print 'Lemma 2.1(iii) and 2.2(iii)', but the left-multiplication criterion is Lemma 2.2(iv), since 2.2(iii) is the finiteness condition. The proofs of Lemma 2.5 and Proposition 2.6 also quote from McConnell-Robson [19, 0.2.6, 2.3.7] that the prime radical of a Noetherian ring is nilpotent and contains every nilpotent ideal, and use without proof that N(Omega(G/J)) = Omega(G/J) intersect N(V(G/J)).

nodes.title: The boundary map K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) -> K_0(M_H(G)) is surjective, and characteristic elements are its preimages
nodes.statement: Under CFKSV's 'Hypothesis on G' (no element of order p, imposed for the rest of their Sec. 3 so that one can work with modules; Lambda(G) then has finite global dimension d+1 by Brumer [4]), the localization sequence of K-theory gives an exact sequence ... -> K_1(Lambda(G)) -> K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) -> K_0(M_H(G)) -> K_0(Lambda(G)) -> K_0(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) -> 0, where the boundary map is denoted partial_G. IF G HAS NO ELEMENT OF ORDER p then partial_G is SURJECTIVE, and one DEFINES a characteristic element of M in M_H(G) to be any xi_M in K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) with partial_G(xi_M) = [M]. The ambiguity in xi_M is exactly the image of K_1(Lambda(G)), by exactness. Moreover, still assuming no element of order p, the natural maps Lambda(G)_S^x -> K_1(Lambda(G)_S) and Lambda(G)_{S^*}^x -> K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) are both SURJECTIVE.
hypotheses: CFKSV prove surjectivity of partial_G : K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) -> K_0(M_H(G)) assuming G has NO ELEMENT OF ORDER p. The same hypothesis underlies their identification of K_0(M_H(G)) through finite global dimension. The hypothesis is NOT necessary for surjectivity in the relative formulation: Kakde Lemma 5 (printed p. 8) proves that partial : K_1(Lambda(G)_S) -> K_0(Lambda(G), Lambda(G)_S) is surjective for every G, 'by the same technique'. Whether the stage's 'vanishing obstruction' is ever nonzero is therefore not settled by these sources. [Corrected in review: the earlier text said surjectivity requires the hypothesis, and identified the stage's obstruction with its failure.]

The proof of surjectivity goes through Lemma 3.5: for P a pro-p open normal subgroup of G, K_0(Lambda(G)) -> K_0(Z_p[G/P]) is INJECTIVE. Its proof uses that Lambda(G) is a free Lambda(P)-module of finite rank and Nakayama for the pro-p P

The first half of Theorem 4.4 uses that Lambda(G)_S is SEMI-LOCAL (Proposition 4.2); Lambda(G)_{S^*} is in general NOT semi-local, and CFKSV exhibit this explicitly for G = Z_p^2, where Lambda(G)_{S^*} has infinitely many prime ideals
Characteristic elements are NOT unique: the definition is a preimage under partial_G
proofSteps: Record the localization sequence (24) for the Ore set S^*.

Lemma 3.5: lift an isomorphism M/IM + Z_p[Delta]^r -> Z_p[Delta]^r along the projective M to a Lambda(G)-map beta; Nakayama on the pro-p P kills the cokernel, and the P-homology of the resulting short exact sequence kills the kernel because Lambda(G) is Lambda(P)-free.

Proposition 3.4 (printed pp. 10-12): lambda = lambda_4 o lambda_3 o lambda_2 o lambda_1 maps K_0(Lambda(G)) to the product over irreducible rho of K_0(L). Here lambda_1 is injective by Lemma 3.5; lambda_2 : K_0(Z_p[Delta]) -> K_0(Q_p[Delta]) is injective by Serre [27, Ch. 16, Thm. 34, Cor. 2]; lambda_3 is injective by Serre [27, Sec. 14.6]; and lambda_4 is an isomorphism (Wedderburn and Morita). Formula (32) expresses lambda through tau([tw_rho(M)]) and the H-homology Euler characteristic epsilon (31). For M in M_H(G), Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 make all H_i(H, tw_rho(M)) torsion, so their classes vanish in K_0(Lambda_O(Gamma)) = Z, which gives lambda([M]) = 0 and hence [M] = 0. Exactness of (24) then gives surjectivity. [Corrected in review: the earlier step mentioned only lambda_1 and lambda_2.]

Evaluation: Phi_rho induces Phi'_rho : K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) -> K_1(M_n(Q_O(Gamma))) = Q_O(Gamma)^x. With phi the augmentation Lambda_O(Gamma) -> O and p its kernel, xi(rho) is defined as phi(Phi'_rho(xi)) if Phi'_rho(xi) lies in the localization Lambda_O(Gamma)_p, and xi(rho) = infinity otherwise (printed pp. 9-10). nodes.title: The conjectural p-adic L-function in K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) with its Artin interpolation, and the main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve, F_infinity = Q(E_{p^infinity}), G = Gal(F_infinity/Q), H = Gal(F_infinity/Q^cyc), Gamma = Gal(Q^cyc/Q), and assume p >= 5 and E has GOOD ORDINARY reduction at p (so that G, a closed subgroup of GL_2(Z_p), has no element of order p). CONJECTURE 5.1: the dual Selmer group X(E/F_infinity) belongs to M_H(G). CONJECTURE 5.7, stated after CFKSV ASSUME the analytic continuation of L(E,rho,s) to s = 1 for all Artin rho and Deligne's period conjecture (103), that L(E,rho,1)/(Omega_+(E)^{d_+(rho)} Omega_-(E)^{d_-(rho)}) is algebraic, and after fixing embeddings of Q-bar into C and Q-bar_p: there exists L_E in K_1(Lambda(G)_{S^*}) such that for all Artin representations rho of G, L_E(rho) is not infinity and L_E(rho) = L_R(E,rho,1)/(Omega_+(E)^{d_+(rho)} Omega_-(E)^{d_-(rho)}) . e_p(rho) . P_p(rho-hat,u^{-1})/P_p(rho,w^{-1}) . u^{-f_rho}, where e_p(rho) is the local epsilon factor at p. Here L_R is the Euler product (104) with the factors at the primes in R removed, R being p together with the primes q with ord_q(j_E) < 0; p^{f_rho} is the p-part of the conductor of rho; 1 - a_p X + pX^2 = (1 - uX)(1 - wX) with u a p-adic unit; and the epsilon factors follow Deligne [10], with local reciprocity sending q to Frob_q^{-1} and the fixed Haar measures and additive characters of printed pp. 33-34. CONJECTURE 5.8 (main conjecture): granted Conjecture 5.7 and Conjecture 5.1, L_E is a CHARACTERISTIC ELEMENT of X(E/F_infinity).
hypotheses: p >= 5 and good ORDINARY reduction; p >= 5 is what guarantees G has no element of order p, since G embeds in GL_2(Z_p)

The interpolation formula carries: a period ratio with the two archimedean periods raised to the multiplicities d_+(rho), d_-(rho); the local epsilon factor e_p(rho) at p; a ratio of local Euler factors at p evaluated at u^{-1} and w^{-1} with the CONTRAGREDIENT rho-hat in the numerator; and a power u^{-f_rho}. When E has CM, Conjecture 5.7 is TRUE and follows from the two-variable p-adic L-function of Manin-Vishik, Katz and Yager; for non-CM E the only evidence is fragmentary numerical data

nodes.title: Kakde's theorem: existence and uniqueness of the p-adic zeta function in K_1' for admissible totally real extensions, under mu = 0
nodes.statement: DEFINITION 1. An ADMISSIBLE p-adic Lie extension F_infinity of a totally real F is a Galois extension with (i) F_infinity/F unramified outside a finite set of primes of F, (ii) F_infinity TOTALLY REAL, (iii) G = Gal(F_infinity/F) a p-adic Lie group, and (iv) F_infinity containing F^cyc. THEOREM 11 (Main Conjecture). Let F_infinity/F be an admissible p-adic Lie extension satisfying the hypothesis mu = 0. Then there is a UNIQUE zeta(F_infinity/F) in K_1'(Lambda(G)_S) such that partial(zeta(F_infinity/F)) = -[C(F_infinity/F)] and, for any Artin character rho of G and any positive integer r divisible by [F_infinity(mu_p) : F_infinity], zeta(F_infinity/F)(rho kappa_F^r) = L_Sigma(rho, 1-r).
hypotheses: p is ODD (stated in the abstract)
F_infinity must be TOTALLY REAL and must contain the cyclotomic Z_p-extension F^cyc
The hypothesis mu = 0 is Iwasawa's conjecture on the vanishing of the cyclotomic mu-invariant for a certain CM extension of the base; it is ASSUMED, not proved

UNIQUENESS holds in K_1'(Lambda(G)_S), NOT in K_1(Lambda(G)_S). K_1' = K_1/SK_1, where SK_1(Lambda(G)_S) is defined as the IMAGE of SK_1(Lambda_O(G)) = inverse limit of ker(K_1(O[G/U]) -> K_1(L[G/U])) (Definitions 6-7, printed p. 9). Kakde warns that 'in all above sources' the zeta function is conjectured to live in K_1, 'and hence uniqueness may not hold'. Those sources are Kato [20], Fontaine-Perrin-Riou [11], Burns-Flach [3], Huber-Kings [17], CFKSV [6], Fukaya-Kato [12] and Ritter-Weiss [29, 32]. The two versions are equivalent because SK_1(Lambda(G)_S) = Ker(partial) intersect (the intersection over Artin rho of Ker(phi' composed with Phi'_rho)), as proved by Burns. [Source list completed in review.]
The interpolation is at rho kappa_F^r with r POSITIVE and DIVISIBLE BY [F_infinity(mu_p) : F_infinity]; not at arbitrary characters
L_Sigma is the Sigma-truncated Artin L-function; the validity of the main conjecture is independent of Sigma as long as Sigma contains all primes ramifying in F_infinity
A COMPLEX C(F_infinity/F) is used rather than the module X = Gal(M_infinity/F_infinity), because when G has elements of order p the module X need not have a finite projective resolution

Kakde's Remark 12 also records the history: the one-dimensional case was considered by Ritter-Weiss [29] and proved in [32] (= arXiv:1004.2578), and 'Using their result D. Burns [2] proved the general case'. Kakde's Sec. 4.1 reduction to dimension one is 'a result of Burns [2] presented differently here'. [Added in review.]

Kakde's framework uses the Ore set S(G,H) inside Lambda_O(G) with O-coefficients and cites CFKSV for its Ore property. CFKSV prove it for Z_p-coefficients only. The O-coefficient extension is not proved in the sources read. [Added in review.]

nodes.title: Leading terms at a representation for elements of localized K_1-groups, and why they are needed
nodes.statement: In the Fukaya-Kato formalism of localized K_1-groups, the p-adic L-function attached to a motive M satisfies an interpolation formula relating, at each continuous finite-dimensional p-adic representation rho of Gal(F_infinity/F), the 'value at rho' to the value at the central critical point of the complex L-function of the rho^*-twist M(rho^*). BUT IF THE SELMER MODULE OF M(rho^*) HAS STRICTLY POSITIVE RANK, BOTH SIDES OF THAT FORMULA VANISH. Burns-Venjakob therefore introduce the notion of 'the leading term at rho' for elements of suitable localized K_1-groups, defined in terms of BOCKSTEIN HOMOMORPHISMS, and prove interpolation formulas for the leading terms of global Zeta isomorphisms attached to certain Tate motives and of the p-adic L-functions attached to certain critical motives. The second of these involves the leading term at the central critical point of the complex L-function, the Neron-Tate pairing and Nekovar's p-adic height pairing.
hypotheses: The formalism is that of Fukaya-Kato's localized K_1-groups together with Nekovar's Selmer complexes and the CONJECTURAL existence of certain canonical p-adic L-functions; so the leading-term statements are conditional on that existence

The vanishing of both sides in positive rank is not hypothetical: Burns-Venjakob cite a result of Mazur-Rubin, itself equivalent to a special case of Nekovar's Theorem 10.7.17, to the effect that positive rank 'should often be the case'

The CFKSV formulation and the Fukaya-Kato formulation have DIFFERENT hypotheses. Burns-Venjakob's paraphrase: CFKSV require Gal(F_infinity/F) to have no nontrivial p-torsion and to contain F^cyc, and the elliptic curve to have good reduction above p with a torsion Selmer group; Fukaya-Kato require only a critical motive with good ORDINARY reduction above p over an arbitrary compact p-adic Lie extension. CAUTION: this paraphrase is looser than CFKSV's printed conjecture. CFKSV Sec. 5 impose p >= 5 and good ORDINARY reduction, and work over Q with F_infinity = Q(E_{p^infinity}) (printed p. 30), so the paraphrase is not a completeness check for NE.0 and NE.5. [Corrected in review.]
The applications are in the setting F^cyc contained in F_infinity

The first application reinterprets the p-adic Stark conjecture at s = 1 (Serre's formulation as interpreted by Tate) as an interpolation formula for leading terms of global Zeta isomorphisms of Tate motives, using Brauer induction together with Deligne-Ribet and Cassou-Nogues

The definition of leading terms via Bockstein homomorphisms is in Burns-Venjakob Sec. 3, which was NOT read; only its description in Sec. 1 (printed pp. 2-3) was read.
